An upstream-closed set of fundamental watersheds holding a watershed group

Source: R/wet_ws_closure.R
wet_ws_closure.Rd

Every polygon whose wscode lies under one of the group's roots, its distinct wscodes with no proper ancestor among them (wet_ws_roots()). FWA_Upstream(a, b) requires b's wscode to lie under a's, so nothing upstream of a polygon in the set lies outside it, and wet_upstream_sums() over the set gives the group's rows (or any row of the set) the sums a whole basin gives them, up to the order the doubles are added in.

Usage

wet_ws_closure(conn, wsg)

Arguments

conn

A DBI connection to an fwapg database.

wsg

Watershed group code, e.g. "BULK".

Value

The polygons in wet_ws_fetch()'s shape, ordered by watershed_feature_id, with attributes wsg, roots (the group's roots), groups (the watershed groups the set spans), codes (the top-level drainage codes it spans) and irregular (the wet_upstream_irregular() pairs of its irregularly coded polygons, to pass as irregular_pairs). Subsetting rows can drop the attributes, so take them first, and cut irregular to the id_up rows kept.

Details

The set is enough, not the least: it holds each root's whole subtree, including the part of a root's stream below the group and its tributaries there. A group holding a polygon whose wscode is a basin root such as 100 gets that whole basin. wet_ws_reach() trims it to the polygons the group's rows reach.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "fwapg")
ws <- wet_ws_closure(conn, "SALR")
attr(ws, "groups")   # LSAL, MUSK and SALR: everything under the Salmon's code
irr <- attr(ws, "irregular")
ws <- ws[wet_ws_reach(ws, ws$watershed_group_code == "SALR", irr), ]
irr <- irr[irr$id_up %in% ws$watershed_feature_id, ]
table(ws$watershed_group_code)   # SALR and two of LSAL's polygons
s <- wet_upstream_sums(ws, "area_m2", irregular_pairs = irr)
s[ws$watershed_group_code == "SALR", ]
} # }
